settings.title: Settings
settings.cliBody: This version of UNCLI is tested with Claude Code {pinned} and downloads its own copy. You can run another version at your own risk.
settings.custom: A custom CLI binary is in use (set by UNCLI_CLAUDE_BIN or the cli.claude.path setting).
settings.risk: Untested versions may change the output UNCLI reads, and answers could stop showing. Return to the pinned version if anything looks wrong.
setup.title: Let's get you set up
setup.lead: UNCLI runs Claude Code for you, without a terminal. It needs its own copy of the CLI and your Claude sign-in.
setup.download.title: Download Claude Code
setup.download.body: Version {version}, from Anthropic, checked against its published checksum. About 240 MB.
setup.signin.title: Sign in to Claude
setup.signin.body: Sign in with your Claude subscription in your browser. The page then shows a code: paste it here.
toolbar.label: Session tools
usage.title: Subscription usage

welcome.title: Welcome to UNCLI
welcome.body: Run several Claude sessions side by side, read answers a page at a time, and never open a terminal.
setup.signin.codePlaceholder: Paste the code from the browser

settings.quickBody: One model for small text jobs outside your sessions, like page summaries. A light model keeps them cheap.
session.moveHint: Drag to reorder, or Alt+↑ / Alt+↓
settings.autoSummaryHint.off: Summarise a page yourself from its outline.

unattended.label: Unattended
unattended.hint: For when you walk away: Claude never prompts you; anything that would have prompted is declined, and Claude is told you're away
unattended.on: You're away: anything that would prompt you is declined, and Claude is told.
mode.label: Prompt me:
why.outside: reaches outside this computer: waits for you
why.none: nothing allows it, so Claude asks
why.complex: too complex for rules ($( ), backticks, braces or file redirects), so Claude asks
rules.sessionTypeNote: These come with the session type. An Unsafe or Blocked entry of yours still wins.
check.title: Check a command
check.label: A command to check
why.inside: UNCLI can't tell, but it stays in this folder (your setting)
why.unknown: UNCLI can't tell, so Claude prompts you (see Settings)
why.judging: UNCLI can't tell: the decision model is checking it
risk.deletes: deletes or overwrites things for good
risk.discards: may throw away changes you haven't committed
risk.outside: changes files outside this session's folder
risk.publishes: sends or publishes something beyond this computer
risk.system: changes system settings or needs admin rights
risk.secrets: touches passwords, keys or other secrets
risk.runs-code: runs code it was handed, which UNCLI can't check
risk.unsure: may not be safe: UNCLI's decision model wasn't sure enough
risk.cloud: changes things in a cloud account
asking.title: Why Claude is asking
asking.unknown: UNCLI can't tell whether this is safe, and your setting is to prompt you about those.
asking.outside: It reaches outside this computer, and you've asked to approve that.
asking.checking: Checking whether a command is safe to run…
settings.unknown.hint: What “Prompt when unsafe” does with a command or tool UNCLI can't place as safe or unsafe.
settings.unknown.inside: Treat it as safe if it stays in this folder
settings.unknown.ask: Treat it as unsafe and prompt me
mode.always.hint: Prompt before anything except reading: edits, commands and other tools all wait for you
mode.unsafe.hint: Reading and safe work just run; Claude prompts you before anything unsafe (deleting for good, publishing, installing, working outside this folder…). Your safe list can change what counts as safe
mode.never.hint: Everything runs without prompting you, except what you've blocked. Questions and plans still come to you
mode.always.on: Claude prompts you before anything except reading.
mode.unsafe.on: Claude prompts you before anything unsafe; reading and safe work just run.
mode.never.on: Claude runs everything without prompting you, except what you've blocked.
scope.label: Where it applies
fixed.inline: It runs code it was handed, so it can't be marked safe: it prompts every time.
fixed.complex: It's too complex to read reliably, so it can't be marked safe: it prompts every time.
fixed.context: It works on files outside this project or on secrets, so it can't be marked safe: it prompts every time.
asking.always: You asked to be prompted before anything except reading.
why.safe: safe: routine work in this folder
why.never: you chose never to be prompted
why.always: you asked to be prompted before anything except reading
trace.allowed.builtin: ran: the session type allows it
teach.hint: Mark {what} as unsafe, so Claude prompts you before it next time
teach.done: Claude will prompt before {what} from now on.
safe.title: Safe and unsafe
safe.body: Your corrections to what UNCLI counts as safe, for {folder} and all projects. Your entries beat UNCLI's own judgement; the most specific one wins, and This project beats All projects.
safe.noSession: Open a session to see the list for its project.
safe.none: Nothing here yet. Use “This is safe” on a prompt, or add a command below.
safe.example: An example command, or a tool name
decider.title: Decision model
decider.body: Decides whether something UNCLI can’t place is safe, when that’s your setting under “When UNCLI can’t tell”. The quick-task model makes these decisions too unless you choose a dedicated decision model, such as Kev (on this computer or your network) or Jev, which gives calibrated answers in a fraction of a second.
decider.quickTask: Use the quick-task model for decisions (default)
decider.systemOne: Use a System One server (Kev, Jev)
decider.versionHint: the version its thresholds are tuned for
decider.localOnly: Only on this computer or my network
decider.keyIsSaved: A key is saved; type a new one to replace it
decider.keyNone: API key (not needed for a local Kev)
safe.labelPlaceholder: What it does, e.g. Deploys the site
approval.undoSafe: Click This is safe again to undo.
settings.notifyBody: A desktop notification when a session you aren’t looking at finishes or needs your approval. Clicking it takes you there.
settings.notify.all: When a session finishes or needs approval
settings.notify.approvals: Only when a session needs approval
settings.editorBody: Code sessions open the files a page lists in your editor, at the line that changed.
settings.editorCommandHint: {file}, {line} and {folder} (the session folder) are filled in. Quote a path with spaces.
settings.editorNotFound: This editor wasn’t found on this computer. Files open with your default app instead.
